# Research: Agentic / generated UI as a product differentiator and user experience
**Date:** 2026-11-09
**Request:** Is "the UI is generated by an agent, live, as you play" a real differentiator for crypt? Five angles: products, agentic UI as a category, games, user-experience evidence, honest differentiation read. Extends research-2026-11-09-generative-ui.md without repeating it.
**Claims investigated:** 5 threads

Verification: "fetched" means I read the page. "search" means search-result summary only; check before quoting. Prior file already holds Leviathan (arXiv 2604.09577), Chen (2508.19227), Jelly, Bernstein, Cifliku, Unbounded, EvoGenUI-Bench; not repeated except where they bear on a verdict.

## Evidence Found

### Thread 1: Products where generated UI is the experience

**Claim**: Consumer products sell generated UI as the experience.
**Verdict**: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Exists in one flagship (Google), framed as an experiment; elsewhere it is a developer feature.
**Sources**:
- Google, Gemini 3 launch, 2025-11-18. "Dynamic view" (Gemini designs and codes a custom interactive response per prompt) and "Visual layout" (magazine-style view with sliders and filters) in the Gemini app, plus AI Mode in Search for AI Pro/Ultra US subscribers (search; Google Research blog fetched). Google's blog: current implementation "can sometimes take a minute or more to generate results"; "occasional inaccuracies"; rater evaluation excluded generation speed (fetched). Verdict: one-shot per prompt, end-user experience, rolled out via A/B test, labelled experiment. Not stateful across a session.
- Vercel v0 and AI SDK 3.0. v0 announced Sept 2023, public beta 2023-10-11, Vercel's own coinage "Generative UI" (search). AI SDK 3.0 streams React Server Components from an LLM into a running app (search). Verdict: developer tool. By 2026 v0's tagline moved from "generative UI" to "Build Agents, Apps, and Websites with AI" (search, tertiary source), so the label is being dropped by its originator.
- Anthropic, Claude generative UI and Artifacts: inline interactive widgets in claude.ai chat, distinct from side-panel Artifacts (search; third-party blogs only, no official page fetched). Verdict: one-shot per message, end-user facing, ephemeral. Feature, not the product pitch.
- OpenAI Apps SDK: third-party developers register MCP-backed apps that ChatGPT renders inline (search; third-party blogs). Verdict: developer integration framework with pre-built components; the model selects, it does not compose.
- tldraw "Make Real" (2023, GPT-4V turns a sketch into HTML in an iframe) and tldraw computer (with Google AI team); Steve Ruiz traces the move from one-shot Make Real to agent loops and multi-agent "fairies" on the canvas (search; Latent Space and AI Engineer talk listings). Verdict: Make Real is one-shot and prototyping; the canvas agents are agentic, but the artifact is a drawing or wireframe, not a live product surface.
**Contradictory evidence**: No consumer product found whose whole pitch is "the interface builds itself." Even Google ships it as an opt-in experiment, and one hands-on piece (Android Authority, search summary; page returned 403) says Dynamic View is slow (up to about 90 seconds) and poor for simple prompts. A search summary states 9 in 10 users never used it; this comes from a secondary blog, unverified.
**Recommendation**: Do not claim the category is proven with consumers. Cite Google as "shipped experiment with latency of a minute or more."

### Thread 2: Agentic UI as a category

**Claim**: "Agentic UI" exists as a named category distinct from one-shot generation.
**Verdict**: SUPPORTED as industry vocabulary and protocols; UNSUPPORTED as an academic category with user studies.
**Sources**:
- Google A2UI, Google A2UI Team, 2025-12-15, spec v0.8 then 1.0, Apache 2.0 (fetched blog). Declarative JSON from a catalog of pre-approved widgets, not executable code. Agent "can efficiently make incremental changes to the UI based on new user requests as the conversation progresses." Adopters named: CopilotKit AG-UI, Opal, Gemini Enterprise, Flutter GenUI SDK. Verdict: agent-driven and stateful across a conversation; developer protocol, not a consumer pitch. Closest architectural match to crypt's engine-owns-state design: the agent emits structure, a trusted client renders.
- AG-UI protocol, CopilotKit, github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui (search). Typed event stream (run start, text, tool calls, state updates) between agent backend and frontend; A2UI 1.0 names AG-UI as a transport alongside A2A and MCP (search). Verdict: agentic, developer protocol.
- Industry definitions (search, all tertiary blogs): doubleslash, DEV Community, The Gradient, Supragent. Common framing: an observe-decide-act loop that rebuilds the interface until the task completes; "agentic UI may use generative rendering as one of its tools." No standard definition; no controlled user study located.
- Jørgensen, Tharmabalan, Aslan, Hansen, Merritt, "Static Vs. Agentic Game Master AI for Facilitating Solo Role-Playing Experiences", arXiv 2502.19519, Feb 2025, "submitted for review" (fetched). ReAct multi-agent GM beats static prompting on modularity, immersion and curiosity. Agentic applies to the GM, not the interface. Prior file had only the title; this verifies it.
- Kim, Min, Xia, Kim, "Elicitive User Interfaces", arXiv 2609.23642, 2026-09-20 (fetched). Two user studies with a design probe: generative UIs that elicit preferences surfaced preferences users had not formed; responses varied more across users than across tasks. Verdict: adaptive/agentic-leaning, research probe.
**Contradictory evidence**: Most "agentic UI" writing is vendor or Medium content. The arXiv papers surfaced (MARLUI 2209.12660, computer-use agent UX 2510.04452, Affora 2609.19125) concern adaptive RL interfaces or agent-facing interfaces, not agent-composed end-user UIs (search only).
**Recommendation**: Use "agentic UI" with a one-line definition; cite A2UI as the nearest concrete spec. Do not cite blogs as evidence of user outcomes.

### Thread 3: Generated UI as a game differentiator

**Claim**: Some game or interactive-fiction product differentiates on an AI-generated interface/presentation.
**Verdict**: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED for scene art and maps; UNSUPPORTED for generated HUD/panels/layout. Confirms and extends the earlier "thin" finding.
**Sources**:
- Slopverse guide, "9 Best AI Text Adventure Games with Pictures (2026)" (fetched). Author discloses he makes Slopverse and ranks it second; facts come from vendor sites, no player reports. Lists per-turn or per-scene image generation: Mythx (Premium only for every scene), Slopverse, Infinite Worlds, LiveTale, FableAI, Wyndra, DreamRunner, Embertold, AI Dungeon ("See" on request, short video). Costs: credits per image or turn; Slopverse admits turns "take a while to play out." Altworld shows a world map; Hidden Door uses hand-drawn art. Verdict: scene illustration is common and pitched as a feature, but the layout is a fixed template (image plus text plus choices). Tertiary, commercially biased.
- AI Adventure mobile app (Google Play listing, search): generated stories and images plus an "Adventure map" of visited places. Closest to generated map plus art; map is a visited-places record, generation method unverified.
- AI Roguelite, Max Loh, Steam, released 2023-10-25 (search). Every entity gets a generated image (local Stable Diffusion or cloud). 83% positive of 618 reviews; reviewers praise the art; complaints are repetition and weak memory/plot, plus no tutorial. Verdict: closest shipped example of generated presentation at play time; image only, UI is fixed. AI Roguelite 2D (sprites) sits at 59% positive of 27 reviews, a thin sample.
- Genie 3, Google DeepMind, announced 2025-08-05 (search): 720p at 24 fps, text-to-navigable world, consistency for "a few minutes." Project Genie opened to AI Ultra subscribers US 2026-01-29, worldwide May 2026, exploration capped at 60 seconds for quality and compute (The Register and others, search). A Medium review: you can walk the world but cannot fight, collect or solve puzzles. Genie 4 announced 2026-10-27 per one search summary, unverified. Verdict: generates the whole world as pixels, not a UI; agentic only in that it is an agent-training environment. Different category from crypt.
- GameUIAgent, arXiv 2603.14724 (search): LLM framework generating editable Figma game UI via a Design Spec JSON and VLM reflection loop. Design-time authoring tool, not runtime. Godmodeai.co "AI Agent for Game UI" Show HN (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45110289, search): design-time export to Unity. Developer tools.
- LLM-as-GM text adventure on Gemini 2.5 Flash (Medium, search): HTML UI whose story pane fills with generated text; layout fixed.
**Contradictory evidence**: A Show HN search for "game generates HUD/panels as you play" found no match (search). Absence of results is weak evidence given search limits.
**Recommendation**: State that runtime image generation is common and generated UI layout is not found in shipped games, with the caveat that coverage was by web search and Show HN scan only.

### Thread 4: What users report about generated, per-moment UI

**Claim**: Users accept a UI that changes per moment.
**Verdict**: UNSUPPORTED for session-long use; supported for one-off pairwise preference only.
**Sources**:
- NN/g, Moran and Gibbons, "Generative UI and Outcome-Oriented Design", 2024-03 (search summary, nngroup.com/articles/generative-ui/). Defines genUI as UI generated in real time per user need and context. Concedes users "could be shown a different UI every time" and designers must balance personalization against lost consistency and predictability. Critic (Marschall-Miller, LinkedIn, search) says NN/g treated this as a footnote; no guaranteed way to return to a familiar UI. Opinion pieces, no data.
- Android Authority, "Gemini's Dynamic View is great, just don't use it for every prompt" (search summary only; fetch 403). Reports waits up to 90 seconds; poor fit for simple prompts. A trade blog reported split user sentiment, "a glorified webpage" (search, secondary).
- Cao et al., Jelly, arXiv 2503.04084 (search). States each prompt revision "may result in a discontinuous transition between generated codebases," hence the persistent task data model. Supports "keep state in a data model the UI is regenerated from," matching crypt's engine-owned state.
- Kim et al. 2026 (above): user studies show preferences vary more across users than tasks.
- "Not Just Novelty", arXiv 2402.09894 (search): three-week study, 12 users, of generative AI tool customization. Small and about tools in general, not generated UI.
- Google figures in a secondary blog (47% preference, 30% fewer steps) conflict with Leviathan's reported 73.5% win and with Google's blog giving no percentages. Treat as unverified.
**Contradictory evidence**: No longitudinal or multi-session study of a model-composed UI found. Pairwise preference studies (prior file) judge static outputs and exclude latency.
**Recommendation**: Say plainly that the session-length experience of a generated UI is unmeasured. Latency (a minute or more at Google) is the best-documented complaint.

### Thread 5: Honest differentiation read

**Claim**: Agentic/generated UI is rare as a shipped user-facing differentiator.
**Verdict**: SUPPORTED for games; PARTIALLY SUPPORTED generally (crowded as developer tooling and protocols, rare as a consumer pitch).
- Crowded: developer frameworks and protocols (v0 and AI SDK, A2UI, AG-UI, Flutter GenUI SDK, Apps SDK), plus chat features (Claude widgets, Gemini Dynamic View).
- Not crowded: a consumer product whose selling point is that the interface assembles itself over a session. Google's own is opt-in, A/B tested, slow.
- Games: many products generate scene art; no product found that generates panels, map layout or HUD composition per moment. AI Adventure (map plus art) and AI Roguelite (per-entity images) are the nearest.
- Nearest analogues for crypt to cite: Google Dynamic View (generated UI as experience, one-shot, slow); A2UI (agent updates UI incrementally across a conversation; the architecture); AI Roguelite and Mythx/LiveTale (generated presentation during play); Genie 3 (generated world, different layer). Crypt's own twin-renderer design (typed data across the wire, client renders) already resembles A2UI's declarative approach, though I did not check crypt docs for this.
- Risk of the framing: the originator of "generative UI" branding (Vercel) moved off the label in 2026 per a tertiary source, and the term now covers anything from a React widget to a world model.

## Research Gaps

**Claim**: A generated, per-moment UI is acceptable over a full session (change aversion, consistency).
**What's missing**: No longitudinal or multi-session study. Only pairwise one-off preference studies and opinion (NN/g).
**Suggested action**: Treat as an open risk; make a session-length playtest crypt's own evidence.

**Claim**: No game generates its UI layout at runtime.
**What's missing**: Absence rests on web searches and one Show HN scan. Steam tag browsing, itch.io, and Hacker News/Reddit threads were not checked. Hidden Door was not checked directly.
**Suggested action**: One targeted pass over itch.io and Steam "AI generated" tags before asserting novelty externally.

**Claim**: Players describe generated presentation as a differentiator.
**What's missing**: Only AI Roguelite Steam review snippets (praise for art) found. No Mythx, LiveTale or AI Adventure player data. Slopverse roundup is vendor-written.
**Suggested action**: Read AI Roguelite and Mythx reviews directly; consider interviews.

**Claim**: Claude and ChatGPT inline generative UI specifics.
**What's missing**: Only third-party blogs. No official Anthropic or OpenAI page fetched.
**Suggested action**: Fetch official docs before citing feature names or dates.

**Claim**: Gemini Dynamic View user reaction and usage figures.
**What's missing**: Android Authority returned 403; 47%, 30% and "9 in 10 never used it" figures come from secondary blogs and conflict with other numbers.
**Suggested action**: Do not quote those figures; read the Android Authority article in a browser.

**Claim**: Genie 4 (2026-10-27) details, Vercel v0 2026 rebrand.
**What's missing**: Single search summaries each.
**Suggested action**: Verify on deepmind.google and vercel.com before use.
